# Vendored runtime dependencies for the installed bundle

This directory is third-party code, committed on purpose. It is not a build artifact and
`npm install` does not create it.

## Why it exists

`claude plugin install ensemble-full` copies the plugin directory. It does not run
`npm install`, so a dependency declared in `packages/full/package.json` is never delivered
to the installed plugin. At 8.1.0 that made four entry points die at load:

```
$ node <installed>/lib/trd-cli.js list --type trd
Error: Cannot find module 'js-yaml'
Require stack:
- <installed>/lib/toolchain/config.js
- <installed>/lib/beads-label.js
- <installed>/lib/trd-cli.js
```

`lib/toolchain/config.js` takes `js-yaml` and `ajv` unguarded at module scope, and
`trd-cli.js`, `toolchain-cli.js`, `beads-label.js` and `complexity-analyzer.js` all require
it. So every command that shells to `trd-cli.js` failed after a clean install.

Guarding those requires is not the fix. `config.js` exists to parse the toolchain YAML and
validate it against a JSON schema, so `yaml = null` turns a clear load-time error into a
null dereference further in.

## Why under `lib/` rather than at `packages/full/`

npm manages a workspace's own `node_modules` and prunes whatever it did not install there.
A tree at `packages/full/node_modules` is deleted by the next `npm install` — measured on
this repo, every package in it to zero in one run. `packages/full/lib/node_modules` is not a
workspace root, so npm leaves it alone.

Node finds it either way. In the installed bundle `lib/toolchain/config.js` is a real file,
so the resolver walks `lib/toolchain/node_modules`, then `lib/node_modules`, and hits this
directory. In this checkout the same path is a symlink into `packages/development/lib/`, and
Node resolves bare specifiers from a file's realpath, so development's own requires keep
resolving through the root `node_modules` as before. The asymmetry is the point: the
checkout and the install each find the copy that is actually there.

## Contents

The closure needed to make every entry point load, seven packages:

| Package | Why |
|---|---|
| `js-yaml` | `lib/toolchain/config.js`, and 14 other sites |
| `argparse` | js-yaml's only dependency |
| `ajv` | `lib/toolchain/{config,runner,validate}.js` |
| `fast-deep-equal`, `json-schema-traverse`, `require-from-string`, `fast-uri` | ajv's `dependencies` |

`uri-js` and `punycode` were here at first, on the assumption that "ajv's closure" meant
every uri package beside it in the root tree. ajv 8.17 resolves URIs with `fast-uri` and
keeps `uri-js` as a devDependency for its benchmarks; `punycode` existed only for
`uri-js`. Removing both and re-running every entry point, plus an ajv `$id`/`$ref`
compile, changed nothing, so they are gone.

`glob` is reached by `skills/core/detect-stack/detect-stack.js` and is not here: that skill
is not an entry point and nothing requires it at load. Adding it is the same exercise if a
command ever needs it, and `validateBundleBareRequires` in `scripts/validate-all.js` fails
if one does.

## Refreshing it

```
rm -rf packages/full/lib/node_modules
npm install                       # ensure the root tree holds the versions you want
node scripts/vendor-bundle-deps.js
```

The script copies each package in the closure from the root `node_modules`, so the vendored
versions always match what the repo resolved and tested against, and it prunes any
directory no longer named in `VENDORED`, so dropping a package is one edit. Commit the
result, and check the diff: it is third-party source and a review should see it change.

`npm run validate` compares every vendored file against that same root tree, byte for
byte, and fails on a mismatch, an extra package or a missing one. `node
scripts/vendor-bundle-deps.js --check` runs that comparison on its own. A version string
is exactly what an altered file leaves untouched, which is why the check reads contents.

## Verifying it

Against the flattened shape, never the checkout — the checkout resolves through the root
`node_modules` and will pass whatever this directory holds:

```
cp -RL packages/full /some/path/with/no/node_modules/above/it
node /some/path/.../lib/trd-cli.js list --type trd      # {"ok":true,...}
```

`npm run validate` does this for every `lib/*.js`.
